items.title: George Masso interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 10, 1997
items.q: It was called a Special Service Band of Europe. Tony Bennett was one of the singers.

ctx.x: Your World War II experience? Were you able to play your music in the Army? Was it the Army?

It was Army, and it was a marvelous experience. In retrospect it was a blessing that I did get into the service. I was inducted while the war was still going on. It was right after the Battle of the Bulge and they threw a lot of us right in the infantry. But by the time I had finished, in fact I was home on leave from infantry basic and the war ended. So I did get shipped overseas, but everything was so loose at that time, and they wanted musicians. I got into a marvelous “band” they called it, but it was an…
I had heard that. That’s interesting.
